# biology-curator skill

Orchestrates a per-paper deterministic parameter extraction campaign.
Consumes a curation manifest YAML, invokes the `param-extractor` skill
per entry, and emits DRAFT cards plus arbitration/not-found queues for
human review.

## When to invoke

When the user wants to populate parameter cards for a published model
in bulk (typically 5 to 500 parameters from a single paper). Examples:
- "Curate parameters for Chassagnole 2002"
- "Run the curator on the Thattai manifest"
- "Re-extract DRAFTs for model X"

Do NOT invoke for single ad-hoc parameter lookups — use `param-extractor`
directly.

## Pre-flight

A curation campaign requires:
1. A manifest YAML (typically generated by `biomodels-manifest` from
   the SBML, then human-pruned & annotated).
2. A cached PDF text in `.paper_cache/` (downloaded by the user; see
   the param-extractor skill for the offline-first rationale).
3. A target cards YAML path under `data/params/`.

## Invocation

```
python tools/curate_params.py \\
  --manifest manifests/<model>.yaml \\
  --output-cards data/params/<model>.yaml \\
  --output-dir data/curation/<model>/
```

Flags:
- `--force` re-extracts DRAFT entries that already exist
  (REVIEWED/APPROVED cards are ALWAYS protected, regardless)
- `--no-biomodels` for offline-only runs

## Outputs

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `data/params/<model>.yaml` | DRAFT cards (RECOMMEND only) |
| `<output_dir>/<model>.needs_arbitration.yaml` | AMBIGUOUS — human chooses |
| `<output_dir>/<model>.not_found.yaml` | NOT_FOUND — human investigates |
| `<output_dir>/<model>.coverage.md` | Markdown report |
| `<output_dir>/<model>.curation_run.json` | Provenance (SHA-256s, timestamps) |

## Hard constraints (enforced by code)

The curator MUST NOT:
- Invent a value not present in the source.
- Auto-promote any card past `DRAFT`.
- Silently resolve an `AMBIGUOUS` extraction — must always queue.
- Overwrite a card whose status is `REVIEWED` or `APPROVED`.

It also MUST:
- Hash every cache file upfront (defense against stale `.paper_cache/`).
- Record per-parameter exit codes in the provenance JSON.
- Be 100% deterministic Python — NEVER an LLM caller.

## Success criteria

A successful run leaves the user with:
1. A clear count of RECOMMEND vs AMBIGUOUS vs NOT_FOUND.
2. Two queue files they can walk through to either arbitrate values or
   investigate misses (the param-extractor manual loop is the next step).
3. A reproducible audit trail (provenance JSON pinning all input hashes).

## Hand-off to review

After curation, the user typically runs:
```
python tools/review_param.py --cards data/params/<model>.yaml
```
to walk DRAFT → REVIEWED → APPROVED with the PDF in hand.

## Shell exit-code gotcha

This CLI returns exit code 0/1/2 to gate downstream steps. If you wrap
it in a script that pipes the output (e.g. `| tee log.txt`), set
`set -o pipefail` first or use `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` — otherwise the pipe
will silently mask the real exit code. See `docs/architecture/shell-exit-codes.md`
for the full set of traps (including PowerShell's interception of `$?`).

## Acceptance test

The Thattai 2001 replay test (`tests/unit/test_curation.py`) demonstrates
all hard constraints. Re-running the curator on a fresh Thattai manifest
must reproduce the k_R card bit-for-bit AND queue the three derived
parameters (gamma_R, k_P, gamma_P) as NOT_FOUND or AMBIGUOUS — never
auto-emit them with invented values.
